title: The Last Oath Revisited
premise: Mara Nystrom has spent her life in the Hollow, a valley where magic cannot follow, trading stolen memories to survive. When a mute child arrives speaking a dead tongue and carrying a shard of the Oathstone—the covenant that once bound the realms together—Mara learns she is the last heir of the Oathkeepers who broke it. Pursued by the Winter Court's heralds and betrayed by the mentor who raised her, Mara must carry the child through the dying lands to the Sundered Gate and reforge the covenant with her own remembered past as the binding material. She succeeds at the cost of surrendering every memory she has ever stolen or lived, ending the long winter but leaving the child—who is revealed to be her younger self, sent back by the reforged covenant—to raise her anew.
about_author: Gideon Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories from isolated mountain communities before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people the maps forgot, and live somewhere with unreliable roads and excellent bread.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Things
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Establishes the Hollow, her memory-thieving trade, and her rule: never steal from children. A routine job goes wrong when she touches a memory that whispers her own name. Emotional beat: restless unease beneath a controlled life.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. During the first unnatural snowfall, a mute girl appears on Mara's threshold, clutching a glowing shard and speaking a language older than any kingdom. The shard burns cold in Mara's hand—and answers her. Emotional beat: dread mixed with recognition.

chapters.title: What the Valley Forgets
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The Hollow's elders demand the child be given to the snow; magic cannot enter the valley, but it can wait at its edge. Mara refuses for reasons she cannot explain. Emotional beat: defiance born of buried instinct.

chapters.title: The Shard Speaks
chapters.summary: Child's fragmented POV, rendered as sensation and image. The shard shows the child visions of a broken gate, a falling winter, and a woman with Mara's face standing in fire. Emotional beat: wordless urgency.

chapters.title: Old Debts
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Her mentor, Corvess, reveals he knew her parents—Oathkeepers who fled into the Hollow to hide their bloodline. He urges her to stay hidden. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under everything she believed.

chapters.title: Heralds at the Edge
chapters.summary: Corvess's POV. At the valley's rim, Corvess meets a Winter Court herald and strikes a bargain: the child for Mara's safety. His rationalization masks old guilt. Emotional beat: love curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: Leaving the Hollow
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Warned by a sympathetic elder, Mara flees with the child the night before the exchange, crossing the boundary where magic floods back into her blood like pain. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration entwined.

chapters.title: First Magic
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Outside the valley, Mara's inherited power awakens violently—she accidentally pulls a memory from a passing soldier and experiences his whole life. The child steadies her. Emotional beat: fear of what she is becoming.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Traveling through petty warlord territories, Mara trades stolen memories for passage, learning how much suffering her gift can ease—or exploit. Emotional beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: A Language Older Than Kings
chapters.summary: Scholar's POV. In the archive-city of Vellum, an aging linguist recognizes the child's speech as Oathkeeper cant, thought extinct. He sends word to interested parties. Emotional beat: scholarly wonder weaponized.

chapters.title: The Hunt Begins
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Heralds in white arrive in Vellum asking after a woman and child. Mara steals a memory from one and glimpses the Winter Court's true aim: not the child, but the heir's willing oath. Emotional beat: hunted clarity.

chapters.title: Corvess Returns
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Her mentor catches up, ostensibly to help, actually to deliver her. The child bites him, and his blood on the shard shows Mara his bargain. Emotional beat: heartbreak sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Memory Thief's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Cornered, Mara could erase Corvess's memories of her and escape clean. Instead she takes only the memory of his bargain, leaving him his love and his shame. Emotional beat: choosing justice over erasure.

chapters.title: Ash Road
chapters.summary: Child's POV, still wordless but growing more articulate. The land worsens—permanent frost, villages burning their furniture to survive. The child begins drawing maps from instinct. Emotional beat: dawning purpose.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Price
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. To cross the frozen river Sere, the ferryman demands a memory of joy. Mara pays with her single recollection of her mother singing. Emotional beat: grief as currency, willingly paid.

chapters.title: Company of Strays
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. They gather followers: a deserter, a hedge-witch whose magic is failing, a boy who remembers nothing at all. Each is drawn to the shard's warmth. Emotional beat: reluctant found-family forming.

chapters.title: What the Hedge-Witch Knew
chapters.summary: Hedge-witch Ilsa's POV. Ilsa recognizes the shard and tells the campfire story of the Oathstone: three realms, one covenant, and the Oathkeepers who shattered it rather than let one realm dominate. Emotional beat: myth becoming history.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Waystone
chapters.summary: Deserter's POV. Heralds attack at night. The deserter dies buying time; Mara, in desperation, pulls the memories out of two heralds' minds, leaving them empty-eyed. Emotional beat: horror at her own capacity.

chapters.title: Empty People
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The hollowed heralds follow them docilely, neither enemy nor ally. Mara must decide whether they are people she wronged or weapons she made. Emotional beat: accountability without absolution.

chapters.title: The Sundered Gate Revealed
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The company reaches the ruins where the Gate once stood—a wound in the world, half-sealed, exhaling winter. The shard fits a socket there but will not turn. Emotional beat: hope meeting impossibility.

chapters.title: Why It Won't Turn
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The Gate requires an Oathkeeper's willing sacrifice—not death, but the surrender of all held memory. Mara realizes the covenant was always paid in identity. Emotional beat: understanding the true inheritance.

chapters.title: The Child's Secret
chapters.summary: Child's POV, now nearly fluent. The child finally speaks plainly: she is Mara, sent back through the reforged covenant from a future where she failed. The shard chose her because she is already Mara's. Emotional beat: revelation as devastating tenderness.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara refuses—if she pays with everything, the woman making the choice dies, and only the child remains. She would rather the winter win than be unwritten. Emotional beat: selfishness examined honestly.

chapters.title: Corvess's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Corvess's POV. Having followed in penance, Corvess offers himself instead—but he is no Oathkeeper, and the Gate rejects him, unmaking him gently. His final memory given freely is of raising Mara. Emotional beat: redemption through useless sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Herald's Offer
chapters.summary: Winter Queen's POV via dream. The Queen appears to Mara in sleep, offering an alternative: swear the child to the Winter Court and live whole, warm, safe. Emotional beat: temptation precisely tailored.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara interrogates the captured herald-minds and learns the original covenant was unjust—that the realms were bound by coercion, and the Oathkeepers were rebels before they were traitors. Reforging means rewriting, not restoring. Emotional beat: the theme crystallizing.

chapters.title: The Company Divided
chapters.summary: Boy-with-no-memory's POV. Some companions want to abandon a suicide mission; others refuse to leave. The boy, who has nothing to lose, argues hardest for going on. Emotional beat: fracture and loyalty tested.

chapters.title: Stealing From Herself
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara experiments: can she give the Gate memories selectively? She practices surrendering pieces of herself, discovering which memories make her who she is—and which merely weigh. Emotional beat: curating a soul.

chapters.title: The Long Night Falls
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Full winter arrives early and total. The company shelters in the Gate's antechamber while frost creeps inward. Ilsa's failing magic gutters out entirely; she gives Mara her staff. Emotional beat: quiet courage before the end.

chapters.title: The Empty Boy's Gift
chapters.summary: Boy's POV. The boy realizes his emptiness makes him a vessel—he can hold surrendered memories safely during the ritual so Mara need not lose everything at once. Emotional beat: the least of them offering the most.

chapters.title: Negotiation With Winter
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara walks out onto the ice to treat with the Queen directly, using stolen herald-memories as leverage. She proposes a new covenant: mutual obligation instead of domination. Emotional beat: a thief negotiating with a god.

chapters.title: The Queen's Wound
chapters.summary: Winter Queen's POV. The Queen reveals her realm is dying too; the broken covenant starves all three worlds. Her cruelty is scarcity. Mara sees an enemy who is also a victim. Emotional beat: enmity dissolving into shared peril.

chapters.title: Terms of the New Oath
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Drafting terms in the old tongue with the child translating, Mara builds a covenant requiring each realm to remember the others—memory itself as the binding law. Emotional beat: authorship of a better inheritance.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Hollowed heralds' collective POV. One hollowed herald, puppeteered by a distant Court faction, attacks during the sealing. The boy takes a killing blow shielding the shard. Emotional beat: cost arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: The Turning of the Stone
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara places the shard, surrenders her hoard of stolen memories first, then her own—one by one, narrated as a life flashing in reverse. The Gate opens. Emotional beat: self-erasure as ultimate act of identity.

chapters.title: Covenant Sealed
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs. Across three realms, winter breaks, magic rebalances, and every mind touched by the new oath feels the others for one heartbeat. The Queen kneels. Emotional beat: awe, world-wide and intimate.

chapters.title: What Remains of Mara
chapters.summary: Child's POV. The ritual leaves a woman with no past—but the boy's vessel holds her core memories, returned imperfectly. Mara wakes knowing she chose this, remembering almost nothing else. Emotional beat: rebirth with gaps.

chapters.title: Homecoming to a Strange Valley
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara and the child return to the Hollow, now reachable by magic, changed forever. The elders who wanted the child given to the snow must meet her as a founder of the new age. Emotional beat: quiet vindication.

chapters.title: Raising Myself
chapters.summary: Alternating Mara/child POV. The two Maras negotiate an impossible domesticity—mentor, mother, mirror. The child begins to forget her future as the timeline heals, becoming simply a girl. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace.

chapters.title: The First Stolen Spring
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, epilogue. Years later, Mara teaches a new generation of Oathkeepers, keeping exactly one theft: a memory of her mother singing, taken back from the ferryman's estate. Spring arrives on schedule. Emotional beat: earned grace.
